tasks.title: Implement TLS Certificate Verification Option
tasks.description: Add an option to enable/disable TLS certificate verification. Default should be enabled.
tasks.details: Modify the configuration to include a boolean flag for TLS verification. Use the `crypto/tls` package to configure the `http.Client` to either verify or skip certificate verification based on the flag. Implement a CLI flag to control this option.
tasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests to verify that the TLS verification option is correctly applied to the HTTP client. Test both enabled and disabled states. Use a mock server with a self-signed certificate to test the disabled state.

subtasks.title: Modify Configuration for TLS Verification Flag
subtasks.description: Add a boolean flag to the application's configuration to control TLS certificate verification. The default value should be 'true' (enabled).
subtasks.details: Update the configuration file format (e.g., YAML, JSON) to include a `tls_verify` field. Ensure the application can read and parse this field.

subtasks.title: Update HTTP Client Configuration
subtasks.description: Modify the `http.Client` configuration to either verify or skip TLS certificate verification based on the `tls_verify` flag in the configuration.
subtasks.details: Use the `crypto/tls` package to configure the `InsecureSkipVerify` field of the `tls.Config` struct. Create a `tls.Config` based on the `tls_verify` flag and apply it to the `http.Client`'s `Transport`.

subtasks.title: Implement CLI Flag for TLS Verification
subtasks.description: Implement a command-line interface (CLI) flag to override the `tls_verify` configuration option.
subtasks.details: Add a CLI flag (e.g., `--tls-verify` or `--no-tls-verify`) that allows users to enable or disable TLS certificate verification when running the application. This flag should take precedence over the configuration file setting. Use a CLI parsing library (e.g., `flag`, `cobra`) to handle the flag.

tasks.title: Implement Environment-Specific Certificate Configuration
tasks.description: Allow users to specify different certificates for different environments.
tasks.details: Update the configuration file format to support environment-specific certificate paths. Modify the application to load the appropriate certificate based on the current environment (e.g., using an environment variable). Use `tls.LoadX509KeyPair` to load the certificate and key.
tasks.testStrategy: Create integration tests to verify that the correct certificate is loaded for each environment. Use different certificates for different environments and assert that the correct certificate is used for each request.

subtasks.title: Update Configuration File Format
subtasks.description: Modify the configuration file format to support specifying different certificate paths for different environments.
subtasks.details: Update the configuration file schema to allow users to define certificate and key paths for each environment. Consider using a nested structure or a key-value pair approach where the key is the environment name and the value is the certificate/key path.

subtasks.title: Load Certificate Based on Environment
subtasks.description: Modify the application to load the appropriate certificate based on the current environment.
subtasks.details: Implement logic to determine the current environment (e.g., using an environment variable). Use this environment information to load the corresponding certificate and key paths from the updated configuration file. Use `tls.LoadX509KeyPair` to load the certificate and key.

subtasks.title: Handle Certificate Loading Errors
subtasks.description: Implement error handling for certificate loading failures.
subtasks.details: Add error handling to gracefully handle cases where the certificate or key file is not found, is invalid, or cannot be loaded. Log informative error messages and potentially provide a mechanism to fall back to a default certificate or abort the application.

subtasks.title: Implement Integration Tests for Different Environments
subtasks.description: Create integration tests to verify that the correct certificate is loaded for each environment.
subtasks.details: Set up different environments (e.g., using environment variables) and configure different certificates for each environment. Run integration tests that make requests to the application and verify that the correct certificate is used for each environment. Assert that the requests are handled correctly with the expected certificate.

tasks.title: Implement Automatic Security Header Addition
tasks.description: Add an option to automatically include security headers in each request.
tasks.details: Implement a configuration option to enable/disable automatic security header addition. If enabled, add headers such as `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Strict-Transport-Security`, and `Content-Security-Policy` with reasonable default values. Allow users to customize these headers via the configuration file.
tasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests to verify that the security headers are added to the request when the option is enabled. Assert that the headers are not added when the option is disabled. Use a mock server to inspect the outgoing requests.

subtasks.title: Implement Configuration Option for Security Headers
subtasks.description: Add a configuration option to enable or disable the automatic addition of security headers.
subtasks.details: Implement a boolean configuration setting (e.g., `automatic_security_headers`) that controls whether security headers are automatically added to each request. This setting should be configurable via the configuration file.

subtasks.title: Add Default Security Headers
subtasks.description: Implement the logic to add default security headers when the configuration option is enabled.
subtasks.details: When the `automatic_security_headers` option is enabled, add the following headers with reasonable default values: `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Strict-Transport-Security`, and `Content-Security-Policy`.

subtasks.title: Allow Customization of Security Headers via Configuration
subtasks.description: Implement the ability for users to customize the security headers and their values via the configuration file.
subtasks.details: Allow users to override the default security header values by specifying custom values in the configuration file. The configuration should allow users to specify the header name and its corresponding value.

tasks.title: Enhance Request/Response Logging Security
tasks.description: Implement secure logging of requests and responses, masking sensitive information.
tasks.details: Modify the logging mechanism to mask sensitive information such as API keys, passwords, and tokens. Use regular expressions or a configuration-based approach to identify and mask sensitive data before logging. Ensure that the logging mechanism is configurable to allow users to control the level of detail logged.
tasks.testStrategy: Create integration tests to verify that sensitive information is masked in the logs. Send requests with sensitive data and assert that the logged output does not contain the unmasked data.

subtasks.title: Identify Sensitive Data
subtasks.description: Identify sensitive data fields (e.g., API keys, passwords, tokens) that need to be masked in logs. Define regular expressions or a configuration-based approach to detect these fields.
subtasks.details: Research and document common patterns for sensitive data. Create a configuration file or define regular expressions to match these patterns. Consider allowing users to add custom patterns.

subtasks.title: Implement Masking Mechanism
subtasks.description: Implement the masking mechanism to replace sensitive data with a placeholder (e.g., '*****').
subtasks.details: Develop a function that takes a string and a list of patterns as input. The function should iterate through the patterns and replace any matching substrings with the placeholder. Ensure the function handles different data types correctly.

subtasks.title: Implement Configurable Logging Level
subtasks.description: Make the logging level configurable, allowing users to control the level of detail logged (e.g., DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR).
subtasks.details: Add a configuration option to specify the logging level. Modify the logging mechanism to filter log messages based on the configured level. Use a standard logging library that supports different logging levels.

subtasks.title: Implement Integration Tests for Masking
subtasks.description: Create integration tests to verify that sensitive information is correctly masked in the logs.
subtasks.details: Create test cases that send requests with sensitive data. Assert that the logged output does not contain the unmasked data. Test different types of sensitive data and different logging levels.

tasks.title: Improve Interactive CLI Interface
tasks.description: Enhance the CLI interface to be more interactive and user-friendly.
tasks.details: Use a library like `github.com/c-bata/go-prompt` to create an interactive CLI. Implement features such as auto-completion, command history, and inline help. Improve the overall navigation and usability of the CLI.
tasks.testStrategy: Manually test the CLI interface to ensure that it is intuitive and easy to use. Verify that the auto-completion, command history, and inline help features work as expected.

subtasks.title: Integrate go-prompt Library
subtasks.description: Integrate the `github.com/c-bata/go-prompt` library into the CLI application.
subtasks.details: Add the `go-prompt` library as a dependency and implement the basic CLI structure using the library's functions.

subtasks.title: Implement Auto-Completion
subtasks.description: Implement auto-completion functionality for CLI commands and options.
subtasks.details: Use the `go-prompt` library to provide auto-completion suggestions based on available commands and options. Define the completion logic for each command.

subtasks.title: Implement Command History
subtasks.description: Implement command history functionality to allow users to access and re-execute previous commands.
subtasks.details: Use the `go-prompt` library to store and retrieve command history. Implement navigation through the history using up/down arrow keys.

subtasks.title: Implement Inline Help
subtasks.description: Implement inline help functionality to provide users with information about available commands and options.
subtasks.details: Use the `go-prompt` library to display inline help messages when the user requests help for a specific command or option. Provide detailed information about each command's usage and available options.

tasks.title: Implement Color Output and Progress Indicators
tasks.description: Add color output and progress indicators to improve the user experience.
tasks.details: Use a library like `github.com/fatih/color` for color output. Implement progress indicators for long-running operations such as sending large requests or processing large responses. Use a library like `github.com/schollz/progressbar/v3` for progress bars.
tasks.testStrategy: Manually test the CLI interface to ensure that the color output and progress indicators are displayed correctly. Verify that the progress indicators accurately reflect the progress of the operation.

subtasks.title: Integrate the `fatih/color` library
subtasks.description: Integrate the `github.com/fatih/color` library into the project to enable color output in the CLI.
subtasks.details: Install the `fatih/color` library.  Modify the CLI output functions to use the library for adding color to the output.

subtasks.title: Implement progress indicators for long-running operations
subtasks.description: Implement progress indicators for long-running operations such as sending large requests or processing large responses using the `github.com/schollz/progressbar/v3` library.
subtasks.details: Install the `github.com/schollz/progressbar/v3` library. Identify long-running operations in the CLI. Implement progress indicators for these operations using the library.

subtasks.title: Ensure correct display of color output and progress indicators in different terminal environments
subtasks.description: Test and ensure that the color output and progress indicators are displayed correctly in different terminal environments.
subtasks.details: Test the CLI in different terminal emulators (e.g., iTerm2, Terminal.app, Command Prompt, PowerShell) to ensure that the color output and progress indicators are displayed correctly. Address any compatibility issues that arise.

tasks.title: Implement Configuration File-Based Default Value Management
tasks.description: Allow users to manage default values for various options via a configuration file.
tasks.details: Use a library like `github.com/spf13/viper` to load configuration from a file. Allow users to specify default values for options such as headers, TLS verification, and logging level. Implement a mechanism to override these defaults via command-line flags.
tasks.testStrategy: Create integration tests to verify that the configuration file is loaded correctly and that the default values are applied. Verify that command-line flags override the configuration file values.

subtasks.title: Integrate spf13/viper Library
subtasks.description: Add the `spf13/viper` library to the project dependencies and set up the basic configuration for its usage.
subtasks.details: Install the `spf13/viper` library using `go get`. Create a basic configuration setup to initialize viper.

subtasks.title: Load Configuration from File
subtasks.description: Implement the functionality to load default values from a configuration file using `spf13/viper`.
subtasks.details: Configure `viper` to read from a specified configuration file (e.g., `config.yaml`). Define the supported configuration options (headers, TLS verification, logging level) and load their default values from the file.

subtasks.title: Implement Command-Line Flag Override
subtasks.description: Implement a mechanism to override the default values loaded from the configuration file using command-line flags.
subtasks.details: Use a library like `flag` or `cobra` to define command-line flags for the configurable options. Implement logic to prioritize command-line flag values over the configuration file values.

tasks.title: Implement History Feature (Previous Request Re-execution)
tasks.description: Implement a history feature that allows users to re-execute previous requests.
tasks.details: Store the history of executed requests in a file or in memory. Implement a command to display the history and allow users to select a previous request to re-execute. Use the `readline` library to manage the command history.
tasks.testStrategy: Manually test the history feature to ensure that it correctly stores and retrieves previous requests. Verify that the re-executed requests are identical to the original requests.

subtasks.title: Store Request History
subtasks.description: Implement the storage mechanism for the request history. This could be in a file or in memory.
subtasks.details: Determine the best storage method (file or memory) and implement the logic to store executed requests. Consider using a data structure like a list or queue to maintain the history.

subtasks.title: Implement History Display Command
subtasks.description: Implement a command to display the history of executed requests to the user.
subtasks.details: Create a command (e.g., 'history') that, when executed, displays the stored request history to the user in a readable format. Consider numbering the history entries for easy selection.

subtasks.title: Implement Request Re-execution
subtasks.description: Allow users to select a previous request from the history and re-execute it.
subtasks.details: Implement the logic to allow users to select a request from the displayed history (e.g., by entering its number). Upon selection, re-execute the chosen request.

subtasks.title: Integrate with Interactive CLI
subtasks.description: Integrate the history feature with the interactive CLI.
subtasks.details: Ensure that the history command is accessible from the interactive CLI and that the re-execution functionality works seamlessly within the CLI environment. Consider using the `readline` library to manage the command history.

tasks.title: Expand HTTP Method Support
tasks.description: Add support for PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, and OPTIONS HTTP methods.
tasks.details: Modify the CLI to support specifying the HTTP method for each request. Update the request sending logic to use the specified method. Ensure that the application correctly handles the different request types.
tasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests to verify that each HTTP method is correctly handled. Send requests with different methods and assert that the server receives the correct method.

subtasks.title: Modify CLI to Support HTTP Method Specification
subtasks.description: Update the command-line interface to allow users to specify the HTTP method (PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS) for each request.
subtasks.details: Implement flags or arguments to specify the HTTP method. Ensure the CLI provides clear error messages for invalid method inputs.

subtasks.title: Update Request Sending Logic
subtasks.description: Modify the request sending logic to use the HTTP method specified via the CLI.
subtasks.details: Update the HTTP client to use the selected method when sending the request. Handle different request body requirements for each method.

subtasks.title: Add Unit Tests for HTTP Methods
subtasks.description: Create unit tests to verify that each HTTP method (PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS) is correctly handled.
subtasks.details: Write tests that send requests with each method and assert that the server receives the correct method and handles the request appropriately. Include tests for different request body scenarios.

tasks.title: Implement Request Chain Functionality
tasks.description: Implement the ability to execute multiple requests sequentially.
tasks.details: Allow users to define a sequence of requests in a configuration file. Implement a command to execute the request chain. Ensure that the requests are executed in the specified order and that the results are aggregated.
tasks.testStrategy: Create integration tests to verify that the request chain is executed correctly. Define a request chain with multiple requests and assert that the requests are executed in the correct order and that the results are aggregated correctly.

subtasks.title: Define Request Chain Configuration File Format
subtasks.description: Define the format for the configuration file that specifies the sequence of requests to be executed in a chain. This should include details like request URLs, headers, bodies, and any environment-specific configurations.
subtasks.details: The configuration file should be easy to read and maintain. Consider using YAML or JSON format. The format should allow specifying the order of requests, request details (URL, headers, body), and any environment-specific overrides.

subtasks.title: Implement Request Chain Execution Command
subtasks.description: Implement the command-line interface (CLI) command to execute a request chain based on the configuration file.
subtasks.details: The command should take the configuration file path as an argument. It should parse the configuration file and initiate the execution of the request chain.

subtasks.title: Ensure Sequential Request Execution
subtasks.description: Implement the logic to ensure that requests within a chain are executed in the order specified in the configuration file.
subtasks.details: This involves iterating through the requests defined in the configuration and executing them one after another. Handle potential errors during request execution and ensure that subsequent requests are not executed if a previous request fails (unless configured otherwise).

subtasks.title: Aggregate Request Chain Results
subtasks.description: Implement the logic to aggregate the results from each request in the chain into a single, comprehensive result.
subtasks.details: This involves collecting the response status codes, headers, and bodies from each request and combining them into a structured format. Consider how to handle errors and provide meaningful information about the overall execution of the request chain.

tasks.title: Implement Response Validation and Testing
tasks.description: Add functionality to validate and test responses against expected values.
tasks.details: Allow users to define validation rules for responses in a configuration file. Implement a mechanism to execute these rules against the response and report any errors. Support validation of status code, headers, and body content. Use a library like `github.com/stretchr/testify/assert` for assertions.
tasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests to verify that the response validation rules are correctly executed. Define validation rules for different response types and assert that the rules are correctly applied.

subtasks.title: Define Configuration File Format for Validation Rules
subtasks.description: Define the structure and syntax of the configuration file for specifying validation rules for responses. This includes defining how to specify rules for status code, headers, and body content.
subtasks.details: The configuration file should be easy to read and maintain. Consider using YAML or JSON format. Define the schema for specifying validation rules for status code (e.g., exact match, range), headers (e.g., presence, exact match, regex), and body content (e.g., JSON schema validation, regex).

subtasks.title: Implement Validation Rule Execution Mechanism
subtasks.description: Implement the core logic to execute the validation rules defined in the configuration file against the actual response received.
subtasks.details: This involves parsing the configuration file, extracting the validation rules, and applying them to the response. Handle different data types and validation methods appropriately. Implement error reporting for failed validations.

subtasks.title: Support Validation of Status Code, Headers, and Body Content
subtasks.description: Implement specific validation logic for status code, headers, and body content based on the defined rules.
subtasks.details: For status code, support exact match and range validation. For headers, support presence check, exact match, and regex matching. For body content, support JSON schema validation and regex matching. Ensure that the validation logic is robust and handles edge cases.

subtasks.title: Integrate with `testify/assert` Library
subtasks.description: Integrate the validation results with the `github.com/stretchr/testify/assert` library to provide clear and concise assertion messages.
subtasks.details: Use the `assert` library to report validation failures with informative messages. Ensure that the assertion messages clearly indicate which validation rule failed and why. This will improve the debugging experience.

tasks.title: Implement Environment Variable Support
tasks.description: Allow users to use environment variables in request URLs, headers, and bodies.
tasks.details: Implement a mechanism to replace environment variables in request URLs, headers, and bodies before sending the request. Use the `os.Getenv` function to retrieve the value of environment variables. Support a syntax like `${ENV_VAR}` to reference environment variables.
tasks.testStrategy: Create integration tests to verify that environment variables are correctly replaced in requests. Define environment variables with different values and assert that the correct values are used in the requests.

subtasks.title: Implement Environment Variable Replacement in URLs
subtasks.description: Implement the mechanism to replace environment variables in request URLs using the `${ENV_VAR}` syntax and `os.Getenv`.
subtasks.details: Implement a function that takes a URL string as input, identifies environment variable placeholders (e.g., `${MY_VAR}`), retrieves the corresponding environment variable values using `os.Getenv`, and replaces the placeholders with the retrieved values. Handle cases where the environment variable is not set (e.g., by logging a warning or using a default value).

subtasks.title: Implement Environment Variable Replacement in Headers and Bodies
subtasks.description: Implement the mechanism to replace environment variables in request headers and bodies using the `${ENV_VAR}` syntax and `os.Getenv`.
subtasks.details: Implement a function that takes a request's headers and body as input, identifies environment variable placeholders (e.g., `${MY_VAR}`), retrieves the corresponding environment variable values using `os.Getenv`, and replaces the placeholders with the retrieved values. Handle cases where the environment variable is not set (e.g., by logging a warning or using a default value).

subtasks.title: Add Integration Tests for Environment Variable Replacement
subtasks.description: Add integration tests to verify that environment variables are correctly replaced in request URLs, headers, and bodies.
subtasks.details: Create integration tests that define environment variables with specific values. Construct requests with URLs, headers, and bodies containing environment variable placeholders. Assert that the placeholders are correctly replaced with the defined environment variable values when the request is sent.
